top_news.title: "Nothing justifies it": Macron condemns "unbridled violence"; announces policy reforms, vows action against rioters
top_news.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday outlined a series of government initiatives to address economic grievances while pledging "uncompromising" legal action against violent rioters following widespread violence and looting across mainland France and its overseas territories. In an address to the nation, Macron announced measures aimed at easing the cost of living, engaging French youth and restoring public order. He also emphasised the need to distinguish peaceful demonstrators from those involved in violence and vandalism. Addressing the soaring cost of living and rising fuel prices,which he attributed to the conflict in the Persian Gulf, Macron announced immediate international efforts to secure energy supplies. He confirmed that he would travel to the Gulf states on Monday morning to discuss securing fuel and gas supplies. "These protesters expressed concern about the cost of living and fuel prices, which stem from the conflict in the Persian Gulf in which France took no part, but whose consequences we bear. I fully understand their concern. It is also being expressed in several other European capitals," he said. "In this regard, I have taken several international initiatives to secure our fuel and gas, and to influence energy markets. I will continue these efforts tomorrow morning by traveling to the Gulf states to secure our supplies. The Prime Minister and the government have also made decisions in coordination with fuel distributors to ensure these efforts are reflected concretely in prices. The government is doing everything possible to address this crucial issue of purchasing power, and I know the French people expect tangible results, and we will continue to act," he added. Acknowledging the "profound anxiety" among high school and university students over their living conditions and future prospects, Macron announced a structured dialogue involving multiple stakeholders, which is scheduled to begin this week. "I understand our high school and university students. They have been at the heart of my political engagement for over ten years. Their voices must be heard, without preconceptions and without downplaying their difficulties," Macron said, adding that "work has already begun within the government. The Minister of National Education took action, launching a platform that gathered over 100,000 contributions, alongside meetings held across regional education authorities and high schools. This will enable us to build tailored solutions together with our youth." To assist business owners affected by the riots, Macron promised immediate financial relief and local security enforcement. "The Prime Minister will chair a crisis unit to deploy aid as quickly as possible and support those enduring these very difficult times," he said, He added that regional prefects will coordinate with local mayors to enforce protective measures, including gathering bans when necessary. Furthermore, Macron instructed the Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu to convene political parties, trade unions, and professional organisations to demand clear public stances against civil disorder. "Everyone must take responsibility. The country needs order, calm, not escalation," Macron affirmed. While offering dialogue to address legitimate economic concerns, Macron issued a stern warning to rioters and those involved in the violence that erupted over the weekend. Denouncing what he termed "unbridled violence" orchestrated by "far-left fringe groups, joined by numerous delinquents," Macron highlighted attacks on civic infrastructure, including the arson of the Limoges town hall, the destruction of Lyon's tourist office, the storming of Marseille's town hall, and an attack on the prefect's residence in Bordeaux. "Nothing justifies it. Nothing explains it. Nothing excuses it. Tonight, we all feel anger, shame," Macron declared, adding, "Towards rioters and anyone engaging in violence, we will be uncompromising. Listening and dialogue mean neither weakness nor impunity." The French President confirmed that the Minister of Justice has instructed public prosecutors to apply the "greatest firmness" in legal proceedings. "Judicial follow-up must be exemplary... Those who destroyed must pay, those who looted must reimburse, and those who sought to bring down the Republic will have to answer for it," he said. articles.title: "Nothing justifies it": Macron condemns "unbridled violence"; announces policy reforms, vows action against rioters
articles.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday outlined a series of government initiatives to address economic grievances while pledging "uncompromising" legal action against violent rioters following widespread violence and looting across mainland France and its overseas territories. In an address to the nation, Macron announced measures aimed at easing the cost of living, engaging French youth and restoring public order. He also emphasised the need to distinguish peaceful demonstrators from those involved in violence and vandalism. Addressing the soaring cost of living and rising fuel prices,which he attributed to the conflict in the Persian Gulf, Macron announced immediate international efforts to secure energy supplies. He confirmed that he would travel to the Gulf states on Monday morning to discuss securing fuel and gas supplies. "These protesters expressed concern about the cost of living and fuel prices, which stem from the conflict in the Persian Gulf in which France took no part, but whose consequences we bear. I fully understand their concern. It is also being expressed in several other European capitals," he said. "In this regard, I have taken several international initiatives to secure our fuel and gas, and to influence energy markets. I will continue these efforts tomorrow morning by traveling to the Gulf states to secure our supplies. The Prime Minister and the government have also made decisions in coordination with fuel distributors to ensure these efforts are reflected concretely in prices. The government is doing everything possible to address this crucial issue of purchasing power, and I know the French people expect tangible results, and we will continue to act," he added. Acknowledging the "profound anxiety" among high school and university students over their living conditions and future prospects, Macron announced a structured dialogue involving multiple stakeholders, which is scheduled to begin this week. "I understand our high school and university students. They have been at the heart of my political engagement for over ten years. Their voices must be heard, without preconceptions and without downplaying their difficulties," Macron said, adding that "work has already begun within the government. The Minister of National Education took action, launching a platform that gathered over 100,000 contributions, alongside meetings held across regional education authorities and high schools. This will enable us to build tailored solutions together with our youth." To assist business owners affected by the riots, Macron promised immediate financial relief and local security enforcement. "The Prime Minister will chair a crisis unit to deploy aid as quickly as possible and support those enduring these very difficult times," he said, He added that regional prefects will coordinate with local mayors to enforce protective measures, including gathering bans when necessary. Furthermore, Macron instructed the Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu to convene political parties, trade unions, and professional organisations to demand clear public stances against civil disorder. "Everyone must take responsibility. The country needs order, calm, not escalation," Macron affirmed. While offering dialogue to address legitimate economic concerns, Macron issued a stern warning to rioters and those involved in the violence that erupted over the weekend. Denouncing what he termed "unbridled violence" orchestrated by "far-left fringe groups, joined by numerous delinquents," Macron highlighted attacks on civic infrastructure, including the arson of the Limoges town hall, the destruction of Lyon's tourist office, the storming of Marseille's town hall, and an attack on the prefect's residence in Bordeaux. "Nothing justifies it. Nothing explains it. Nothing excuses it.
